title: Telling Stories with Python

content.title: Strings are text
content.summary: Text inside quotes is displayed exactly as written.
content.body:
In Python, text inside quotation marks is called a string.

Strings can contain letters, numbers, spaces, punctuation, and even emoji. Python displays them exactly as you type them.

Strings are how programs display words and messages on the screen.

content.title: Multiple print() lines
content.summary: Every print() creates a new line in the output.
content.body:
You can write as many print() lines as you want.

Every time Python runs a print() command, it creates a new line in the output.

Programs are like a list of instructions — Python follows them one by one.

content.title: Stories have an order
content.summary: Python runs from top to bottom — changing the order changes the story.
content.body:
Python always starts at the first line and works its way down.

That means the order of your print() lines matters. If you move lines around, your story changes too.

Each print() line is like one moment in your story.

content.title: Try experimenting
content.summary: There is no single correct story.
content.body:
Try changing the story completely.

Funny stories, dramatic stories, strange stories, and random stories all work. Programming is not just about following instructions — it's also about creating things.
